selection: All eight Scrapy training candidates assigned to the broad incomplete-case, state-transition or context-propagation discovery leaves at this checkpoint; this repository has no state-transition candidates in those leaves.
interpretation: These are separate mechanism, contract, context, security and experimental-subset proposals, not approved labels, a taxonomy freeze or independent issue identities. Existing discovery labels remain broad where no existing narrow definition fits. A conditional context proposal is not numerical-budget or tool feasibility certification.

reviews.mechanism: Whole-field equality is used where media-type identity excludes case differences and optional parameters.
reviews.taxonomy_boundary: Do not force this into delimiter parsing: that leaf concerns a separator wrongly applied across accepted formats. This is token/field identity normalization before gzip classification; retain the broad discovery leaf until a justified narrow definition is proposed.
reviews.contract_reason: The old predicate already recognizes application/gzip and application/x-gzip. Retained regression adds parameterized and mixed-case forms of those same media types, rather than a new compression format.
reviews.context_reason: The whole-header comparison and existing media types are visible. Ordinary Content-Type semantics suffice to identify missed case/parameter forms; a live decompressor or helper is not needed for this narrow classification finding. A common input/runtime protocol and faithful after-side helper representation remain unfrozen.
reviews.security_reason: The witness is misclassification of a valid response media type. No selected evidence establishes a decompression limit bypass, attacker privilege change or security-enforcement consumer. Do not infer security safety for downstream untrusted response processing.
reviews.negative_reason: The retained parameterized/mixed-case witnesses are addressed by the new external regex. Its word-boundary prefix is not a complete MIME-token grammar: punctuation-bearing tokens beyond gzip require separate review. No regex or compressed data was evaluated.
reviews.subset_reason: A narrow before-only classification finding is locally supportable using ordinary media-type semantics; admission still depends on the common protocol and researcher confirmation.
reviews.dependence_reason: Keep the existing family. Other fixes in scrapy/utils/gz.py, including scrapy-11, are version/context links rather than automatic same-root-cause merges.
open_questions: Freeze the intended MIME-identity finding and treatment of residual after-side token overacceptance.
Confirm the common input budget and non-security scope without adding response consumers to selected-function input.

reviews.mechanism: An absent status-table key becomes None and is passed to a string-only converter before retry dispatch.
reviews.taxonomy_boundary: Do not call this missing-label validation: CORR-LOOKUP-VALIDATION requires rejecting absent labels, whereas this established operation must tolerate an unknown numeric status. The causal defect is a missing fallback at a partial lookup/conversion boundary, not cosmetic wording.
reviews.contract_reason: Retained fix message and numeric 573 regression require a usable description for nonstandard status codes. Newly pinned pre-fix retry middleware calls this helper before scheduling a retry, and the exact pre-fix converter rejects None in both Python2 and Python3 branches.
reviews.context_reason: The before function does not define the imported response table or to_native_str. A missing dict default is visible, but inferring a failing rather than permissive None conversion critically depends on that project's converter. The caller establishes that description failure interrupts retry; it cannot be silently added to detection input.
reviews.security_reason: The established witness is retry reliability for a configured nonstandard status. Untrusted HTTP responses alone do not establish a security availability boundary or attacker-induced harm threshold. Retain this distinction from a proven denial-of-service label.
reviews.negative_reason: Adding a string fallback avoids None conversion for absent numeric keys. Nonnumeric inputs, a customized response-table mapping and exact deployed Twisted versions are not certified. The exact table entry for 573 is not pinned here; the retained regression documents the expected unknown case.
reviews.subset_reason: Propose deferring this pair from the strict before-only primary subset unless the common ordinary-API policy can justify the imported converter without project-specific evidence. The functional mechanism remains supported in adjudication context.
reviews.dependence_reason: The retry consumer is context for the same witnessed helper failure, not another independent observation or newly admitted pair.
open_questions: Confirm the actual Twisted status mapping/version if an exact unknown-code witness is required.
Resolve the uniform ordinary-API versus project-helper boundary before primary-subset admission.

reviews.mechanism: A tolerated None domain is passed to a string regex before the same function's later None filter.
reviews.taxonomy_boundary: CORR-NULL-BOUNDARY describes missing structural neighbours/sentinels and dereference, not arbitrary optional collection elements passed to a string matcher. Retain a precise descriptor instead of broadening that leaf without a versioned definition change.
reviews.contract_reason: The before function already filters None in its domain comprehension; the retained commit explicitly restores existing None-entry behavior/tests. Thus a None guard is not inferred solely from a newly added test or a new URL-entry policy.
reviews.context_reason: The before function exposes both the None-tolerant comprehension and the earlier match call. Standard Python re string-type semantics establish the local TypeError without a caller. This does not establish a security policy or runtime-specific warning behavior.
reviews.security_reason: The same file builds an offsite policy, but its output consumer explicitly bypasses that filter for request.dont_filter and otherwise applies a hostname regex. A crawler navigation policy is not automatically a security sandbox. Deployment trust, user-controlled policy/requests and security promises remain unestablished.
reviews.negative_reason: The None-plus-valid-domain witness is guarded. All-invalid domain lists, empty hostname handling, URL-entry omission and dont_filter bypass are separate behaviors; do not label the resulting crawler safe or the function universally clean.
reviews.subset_reason: Local function-only observability is plausible, but defer final non-security/security subset placement until the policy trust boundary is explicitly resolved.
reviews.dependence_reason: Keep one mechanical family for this policy-builder fix; helper/consumer references are not independent issues. URL-entry changes in the same function must not inherit the None witness automatically.
open_questions: Determine whether offsite filtering is promised as navigation convenience or a security boundary in the intended use.
Review all-invalid/empty-host behavior separately, without executing the regex.

reviews.taxonomy_boundary: Keep context propagation as the causal leaf: the wrong base is supplied upstream. Do not replace it with URL-composition merely because the eventual symptom is a destination, or merge the companion _get_form_url diff into the same selected positive without attribution.
reviews.contract_reason: The retained base-tag regression requires a relative action to resolve against b.com rather than the response a.com. The pinned helper explicitly obtains document-base context, and the same archived file shows _get_form feeding request URL construction.
reviews.context_reason: The selected function passes response.url, but whether create_root_node/lxml already applies HTML base semantics is not defined in that function. Its helper and downstream action handling are critical to attributing this observed destination defect rather than guessing from a changed argument.
reviews.security_reason: The retained expected result intentionally allows a cross-origin HTML base. Correct destination resolution is not an SSRF, same-origin or CSRF enforcement claim. Selector-argument interpolation elsewhere in the unchanged function needs separate input-provenance analysis, not a transferred security label.
reviews.negative_reason: The explicit base-tag/relative-action witness is addressed through the document-base helper. Its first-4096-character scan, dependency versions and other selector/formnumber paths remain limitations; not universal HTML/request correctness.
reviews.subset_reason: Defer strict before-only admission until the common API/context rule resolves the missing root-builder and action semantics; adjudication evidence must remain outside detection inputs.
reviews.dependence_reason: Retain the same mechanical family as _get_form_url, whose current discovery decision is proposed exclusion. That sibling's URL-join rewrite does not prove an independent old failure; preserve both canonical IDs and separate eligibility proposals.
open_questions: Pin actual parsel/lxml versions if needed beyond the versioned comparison evidence.
Resolve the 4096-character base scan limitation and a consistent strict-function-only subset decision.

reviews.mechanism: An optional unbounded-capacity sentinel is used directly in an ordered numeric comparison before insertion.
reviews.taxonomy_boundary: Neither a missing collection neighbour nor a numerical zero denominator: do not force this into NULL-BOUNDARY, EMPTY-SEQUENCE or arithmetic-zero leaves. The relevant contract is limit=None as a capacity sentinel, with Python-version-specific comparison behavior.
reviews.contract_reason: The archived pre-fix constructor defaults limit to None and stores it unmodified; the setter cannot fulfill that existing default on Python3. Retained tests exercise both positive finite capacity and default unbounded insertion.
reviews.context_reason: The before setter alone does not show self.limit's domain or default. Assuming None is a valid sentinel requires the omitted constructor. A common runtime declaration alone does not supply that missing object invariant.
reviews.security_reason: Unlimited mode is the existing constructor default, not a proven attacker-controlled disabling of a required resource bound. No trust/reachability or memory-security claim follows from cache terminology.
reviews.negative_reason: The default None witness is guarded on Python3. The truthiness guard also treats zero as unbounded; negative limits and replacement of an existing key in a full cache remain unresolved behaviors, not covered negatives.
reviews.subset_reason: Defer strict selected-function-only admission because the required None-valued invariant is outside this function. Preserve the contextual supported mechanism for a separately specified common-context condition if one is later approved.
reviews.dependence_reason: The constructor is evidence for this selected setter, not another counted pair. Preserve the family and repository dependence; no audited independent issue identity is assigned.
open_questions: Confirm explicit zero/negative capacity policy and existing-key eviction behavior before any wider paired-negative claim.
Resolve a common treatment of missing object invariants without selectively adding constructors.

reviews.mechanism: Command discovery calls a Python2-only dict method on the ordinary dict returned by vars(module).
reviews.taxonomy_boundary: A runtime API-compatibility mechanism, not a missing dispatch case in an already supported runtime. No existing narrow leaf should be expanded merely to keep this broad category supported.
reviews.contract_reason: New exact pre-fix setup.py lists Python2/2.7 and installation documentation assumes Python2.7. The fix re-enables previously ignored Python3 tests, leaving compatibility-development work versus a prior support promise unresolved. This prompted appended discovery revision2, supported to ambiguous; absence of a classifier alone is not proof of non-support.
reviews.context_reason: With Python3 specified uniformly, vars(module) returns a dict lacking itervalues, so the local failure follows from ordinary API semantics. The selected function cannot establish that Python3 was an existing supported runtime, and on documented Python2.7 the method exists.
reviews.security_reason: The witness is runtime command-enumeration failure, not unauthorized plugin loading. Module walk/import and plugin trust assumptions are separate, unexecuted context.
reviews.negative_reason: values() addresses the Python3 missing method but is not an established positive-to-negative repair on Python2.7. Whole command execution, plugin imports and separate subprocess-test byte changes are outside scope.
reviews.subset_reason: No admission until the prior-runtime support obligation is evidenced. Preserve ambiguity rather than declaring a feature exclusion solely from missing metadata or treating re-enabled tests as a retrospective contract.
reviews.dependence_reason: Retain the current mechanical family and original source pair; the associated testproc byte conversion is not a second selected positive here. Runtime/version dependence does not establish an independently adjudicated issue.
open_questions: Find an explicit pre-fix Python3 support commitment or a documented experimental-runtime eligibility policy.
Freeze a common declared-runtime policy without metadata leakage into function input.

reviews.mechanism: Initialization forwards the original sparse settings dict after its superclass has constructed the canonical default-populated settings object.
reviews.taxonomy_boundary: Context propagation is the evidenced causal leaf; do not replace it with configuration precedence because no competing override wins here. Do not exclude it as diagnostic-only: argument construction indexes a required default key before logging.
reviews.contract_reason: The archived pre-fix superclass explicitly accepts dicts and sets self.settings. The retained sparse-dict regression checks defaults. The pinned unchanged log_scrapy_info indexes BOT_NAME, whereas configure_logging separately normalizes dicts, so their failure paths must be distinguished.
reviews.context_reason: The five-line before constructor does not expose superclass normalization or the logging consumer's required keys. It does not locally prove that passing settings is wrong or that self.settings is canonical; both external contracts are necessary.
reviews.security_reason: The retained witness is initialization KeyError for an accepted sparse dict. No leak, unauthorized configuration override or sensitive-log disclosure is demonstrated by this fix.
reviews.negative_reason: Using canonical settings addresses default-key availability for the witnessed initialization path. Arbitrary settings objects, other logging side effects and all constructor/shutdown behavior are not certified.
reviews.subset_reason: Defer strict before-only admission because essential producer/consumer contracts are omitted. Preserve the contextual defect and do not import superclass/helper evidence into one condition selectively.
reviews.dependence_reason: The two logging calls are changed in one selected constructor and one mechanical family. Only the consumer-specific witnessed failure is attributed; two calls do not imply two independent issues.
open_questions: Confirm the exact Settings/default source chain if more than the retained sparse-dict witness is claimed.
Apply the same missing-producer/consumer rule to all supported context-propagation cases.

reviews.mechanism: The clickable-control enumeration omits image inputs, which the ordinary input enumeration already excludes.
reviews.taxonomy_boundary: Retain an explicit enumeration-partition descriptor. CORR-RULE-APPLICABILITY concerns correction rules firing in the wrong command state, not arbitrary missing HTML controls; no automatic relabelling into that leaf.
reviews.contract_reason: The selected helper promises to choose clickable controls; image inputs are ordinary submit controls. Its archived sibling excludes image from ordinary values and appends this helper's choice. The retained image-only name/value regression documents the intended result, not image-coordinate conformance.
reviews.context_reason: Under ordinary HTML image-submit and XPath semantics, the selected before selector has no image alternative and returns early without a candidate. This is a local missing-control finding. The wider dropped-form-field manifestation needs _get_inputs context, and exact lxml selector/version feasibility remains to be confirmed.
reviews.security_reason: The witnessed mechanism is a missing successful form value. The unchanged clickdata XPath interpolation has a separate possible interpretation-boundary question requiring caller input provenance; this fix does not establish either a security defect or clean XPath handling.
reviews.negative_reason: The image-only default-click name/value path is added. Image x/y coordinates, nr selection through form.inputs, arbitrary clickdata XPath, override precedence and browser-equivalent submission remain outside this narrow negative.
reviews.subset_reason: A local omitted-control finding can be proposed under a uniformly defined ordinary HTML/XPath API policy. Do not require the model to infer the complete external form-value loss or grant it the regression answer.
reviews.dependence_reason: Keep this distinct mechanism from earlier form-base, whitespace and redirect fixes in the same evolving helper file. Shared file/function versions organize dependence review but do not imply a common root cause.
open_questions: Confirm the common ordinary-API policy for HTML/XPath and actual dependency representation.
Retain explicit mechanism-local negatives rather than full browser submission or security-clean labels.
